title: Russia 232-Drone + 1 Ballistic Missile Overnight Attack — 217 Intercepted; 14 Regions Struck on Day 1,556
detail: Overnight into May 30, 2026 (Day 1,556), Russia attacked Ukraine with 232 attack drones and 1 ballistic missile. Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 217 of the 232 drones. Hits were recorded across 14 Ukrainian regions. In the broader 24-hour period, Russia conducted 1 missile strike (7 missiles), 91 airstrikes, and dropped 277 guided aerial bombs, deploying 8,549 kamikaze drones total. Russian losses for the day: approximately 1,430 personnel, 2 tanks, 7 armored vehicles, 70 artillery systems, 5 MLRS, 1,781 UAVs, and 483 vehicles. The front line saw 291 combat engagements, with the Pokrovsk sector recording the highest activity. The attack continued Russia's near-nightly Shahed drone campaign that has averaged 100–300+ UAVs per night throughout May 2026.

media.caption: Russia 232-drone + 1 ballistic missile overnight attack — 217 intercepted, 14 regions struck; 291 combat engagements on Day 1,556

title: Ukraine Overnight Deep Strikes: Taganrog Port, Armavir Oil Depot, Yaroslavl Fuel Tanks, Volgograd Refinery Halted — $9.5B+ Energy Campaign
detail: On May 29-30, 2026 (Day 1,556), Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces conducted coordinated overnight deep strikes against multiple Russian energy targets: (1) Taganrog, Rostov Oblast — drones struck a tanker, fuel storage tanks, and an administrative building at the port, sparking a major fire; 2 civilians injured when a drone hit a private home; (2) Armavir, Krasnodar Krai — oil depot set ablaze, approximately 500 km from Ukraine's border, demonstrating expanded deep-strike reach; (3) Yaroslavl — giant fuel storage tanks burned after drone strikes; (4) Volgograd — oil refinery forced to halt operations following drone strikes. Additionally, Ukraine struck a Russian shadow-fleet tanker and a marine oil terminal in occupied Crimea in coordinated overnight operations. Zelensky confirmed the Armavir strike in his nightly address. These strikes are part of Ukraine's sustained 2026 deep-strike energy campaign that has cost Russia an estimated $9.5B+ in energy sector losses since January, including prior strikes on Tuapse (x4), Kirishi, Ryazan (x3), Syzran, Astrakhan, Yaroslavl, Kstovo, and the Moscow region.

media.caption: Ukraine drones strike Taganrog port tanker and fuel storage, Armavir oil depot, Yaroslavl fuel tanks, and Volgograd refinery overnight — part of 2026 energy campaign costing Russia $9.5B+

title: Zelensky Warns Russia Planning 'Massive' New Attack + Possible Northern Ukraine Offensive — Meets Budanov, Umerov; Writes to Trump on Patriot Shortage
detail: On May 30, 2026 (Day 1,556), President Zelensky issued dual warnings: (1) that intelligence indicates Russia is preparing a new 'massive attack' against Ukraine; and (2) that Russia may be planning a northern Ukraine offensive, raising fears of a new front or a push from the Belarus or Sumy direction toward Kyiv. Zelensky held a strategic meeting with intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov, Energy Minister Shmygal, and National Security Council Secretary Umerov to assess threats and discuss air defense resupply. Ukraine faces a critical shortage of Patriot intercept missiles after the intense May 2026 barrage season. Zelensky sent an urgent letter to President Trump warning of the Patriot shortage. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth separately told reporters that Washington would 'find a way' to help Ukraine defend itself. Zelensky also announced 'important upcoming negotiations' but declined to name participants or timing — potentially referencing future peace talks. The EU-Ukraine Support Loan ratification (€90B, bill No. 0376) was also cited as urgently needed for defense procurement.

media.caption: Zelensky warns Russia is preparing a massive new attack and possible northern offensive — meets Budanov and Umerov; writes to Trump on critical Patriot missile shortage
